title: Isolation and detection of extracellular vesicles from melanoma cells and liquid biopsies using size-exclusion chromatography and nano-flow cytometry
protocol: Test the cells for mycoplasma contamination.
Culture melanoma cells in a 150 cm² flask with pre-warmed cell culture medium for maintenance.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Aspirate cell culture medium from the cells.
Add 10 mL PBS and slightly sway the flask.
Immediately remove PBS.
Repeat steps of adding and removing PBS two more times.
Add 25–30 mL of "cell culture medium for EV collection" and grow the cells in a cell incubator for 48–72 hours.
Collect the cell supernatant by pipetting it into a 50 mL conical tube.
Cool down centrifuge to 4°C prior to processing and concentration of cell culture supernatants.
Centrifuge the 50 mL conical tubes containing approximately 25-30 mL of cell culture supernatant (500 g, 5 min, 4°C) to remove cellular debris.
Carefully pipet the cell culture supernatant into a new 50 mL conical tube without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge the collected cell culture supernatant (3000 g, 20 min, 4°C) to remove larger microvesicles and enrich for smaller MVs and exosomes.
Carefully pipet the cell culture supernatant into a new 50 mL conical tube without touching the pellet.
Filter the collected melanoma cell culture supernatant through a 0.45 μm PES filter using a syringe.
Wash Amicon Ultra-15 filter units with PBS by adding 15 mL of PBS and centrifuging until the PBS passes through (4000 g, 3 min, 4°C).
Accurately balance Amicon Ultra-15 filter units in the centrifuge to prevent damage.
Decant the PBS after centrifugation.
Pipette 15 mL of processed cell culture supernatant onto the filter.
Centrifuge (4000 g, 6 min, 4°C) until 500 μL of concentrated supernatant remains in the filter unit.
Discard the flow-through by decanting.
Repeat steps 13–16 with the rest of the cell culture supernatant to obtain a final volume of 500 μL of concentrated cell line supernatant.
Transfer 500 μL of the concentrated melanoma cell line supernatant into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge blood collected in plasma and serum collection tubes immediately upon blood draw at 1600 g for 10 minutes at 22°C.
Use wide-bore (wide orifice) pipette tips to reduce shear forces on the sample during handling.
Process blood samples immediately after blood draw to ensure reproducibility.
Store excess plasma or serum at -80°C after preprocessing.
Transfer plasma or serum supernatants into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Perform a second centrifugation step (3000 g, 10 min, 22°C) and transfer the plasma or serum into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Cool a microcentrifuge to 4°C for processing of blood liquid biopsies.
Thaw frozen plasma or serum samples on ice for 30 minutes if needed.
Pipette 250 μL of the plasma or serum into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 10,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge plasma or serum into a microcentrifuge at 10,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube without touching the pellet.
Sterilize DPBS through a 0.2 μm membrane filter.
Degas the buffer with a vacuum pump for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Prepare an appropriate column holder/rack and align pre-labelled collection tubes in order of elution.
Remove the top column cap once the column has reached operational temperature.
Attach the IZON qEV original (70 nm) column to the column holder.
Insert the buffer reservoir on top of the column.
Prepare a container for collecting DPBS washes.
Remove the bottom column cap and allow buffer to run through the column matrix into the collection container.
Add 20 ml of degassed DPBS on top of the column once the last drop has run into the filter.
Wash columns with 20 mL of degassed DPBS.
Add the sample to the column: Carefully pipette 500 μL processed and concentrated cell culture supernatant onto the column and let the void volume flow into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube below the column.

Or add plasma or serum samples: Carefully pipette 200 μL of processed plasma or serum onto the column. As soon as the sample has run into the frit, add 300 μL of degassed DPBS and let the void volume flow into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube below the column.

Wait until the entire sample volume has been absorbed by the column, then add another 500 μL of degassed buffer onto the column and continue to collect the void volume into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat step 36 collecting eluting 500 μL fractions in separate 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Determine the EV-containing fractions using nano-flow cytometry, nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), or similar methods for specific experimental conditions.
When running more than one sample on a column, wash with at least 20 mL of DPBS between samples.
Rinse the column with 5 mL of 0.5 M NaOH when required.
Wash the column with 30–40 mL of DPBS and measure pH to check if the wash was sufficient.
Pool EV-containing fractions (e.g., fractions 7–10) for further downstream processing.
Determine particle concentration and size of different fractions when working with a new cell line.
Store obtained EV-containing fractions at 4°C for downstream analysis within the next 24 hours.
Freeze EV-containing fractions at -80°C for long-term storage.
Prepare NanoFCM Quality Control Nanospheres (QC bead) solution as a concentration standard and for initial system alignment by adding 1 μL QC beads in 99 μL deionized water.
Add 1 μL of size calibration beads in 99 μL deionized water in a 0.6 mL MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube.
Prepare the cleaning solution by adding 150 μL Nano FCM cleaning solution in a 0.6 mL MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube.
Add 100 μL of DPBS in a 0.6 mL MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube as a negative control for background correction.
Thaw the experiment samples on ice while performing nanoFCM setup.
Start-up and initialize the fluidics of the NanoFCM machinery.
Switch on the single-photon counting modules (SPCM) detector once the fluidics are initialized.
Load the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the QC bead solution into the machine.
Boost the QC bead solution for 45 seconds prior to data acquisition.
Align the lasers until optimal signal intensities/events for side scatter are achieved.
Ensure intensity histograms represent a uniform and narrow peak during alignment.
Adjust horizontal and vertical position of optical lenses if necessary.
Optimize laser focusing lens alignment by turning knobs.
Switch to “auto-sampling” mode to keep pressure stable throughout use.
Set auto-sampling pressure range between 0.4–1.5 kPa.
Acquire QC beads for 1 minute and save data as an NFA file manually.
Unload the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube containing QC bead solution.
Load the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with cleaning solution.
Boost the cleaning solution for 45 seconds.
Remove the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with cleaning solution from the inlet.
Briefly dip the inlet in a MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with deionized water to clean the sample line.
Load the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the size bead solution.
Boost for 45 seconds.
Acquire the size bead solution for 1 minute and save the data as an NFA file.
Unload the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the size bead solution.
Repeat the washing steps (51–53).
Load the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with filtered DPBS.
Boost for 45 seconds.
Acquire PBS for 1 minute and save the data as an NFA file.
Unload the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with PBS.
Repeat the washing steps (51–53).
Load the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the sample.
Boost for 45 seconds.
Acquire the sample for 1 minute and save the data as an NFA file.
Unload the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the sample.
Repeat the washing steps (51–53) before measuring the next sample.
Load again the MaxyClear Snaplock microcentrifuge tube with the QC bead solution.
Boost the loaded tube for 45 seconds.
Acquire the QC bead solution for 1 minute and save the data as an NFA file.
Check that the recording of the QC bead solution is comparable to the initial acquisition.
Shut down NanoFCM.
Click on "Count STD" to set the standard.
Open the file with the acquired size beads.
Automatically set the threshold by clicking on "AUTO".
Manually alter the baseline using the "Signal Processing Control" tab if required.
Set the side scatter channel intensity to 35 when the blank level of the side scatter channel is ∼70.
Open the calibration panel “Size MESF” and choose the S16M-exo standard to fit the curve.
Click on “find peak”.
Open the file with the acquired DPBS sample.
Automatically set the threshold for DPBS by clicking on "AUTO".
Click on "Count Blank" to set the background.
Save the DPBS background (size distribution window “B”) to the settings.
Open the file with sample data.
Subtract the saved DPBS background from the sample with blank correction (size distribution window “BC”).
Export the quantified data as a size and concentration report.
Export the file as a PDF report.
Include information about sample size distribution (nm) and particle concentration (particles/mL).
Adjust the concentration of the beads by entering the concentration of the QC beads used.
Enter your sample dilution to calculate the final particle concentration.
Save the files as FCS files for analysis in alternative programs like FlowJo.
Ensure that FCS files are exported with applied thresholds.
Data points below the threshold will be lost.
Acquire samples including blank control with the same instrument settings and thresholds set during analysis.
